title: Lobster Bisque
subtitle: Creamy French seafood soup from roasted lobster shells
excerpt: The great French shellfish soup: lobster shells roasted until golden, then simmered with cognac, white wine, and aromatic vegetables into a rich, orange-hued stock, blended and enriched with cream until silky and intensely flavoured.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bisque is a cream-based shellfish soup of French origin, traditionally made from crustaceans: lobster, crab, crayfish, or shrimp. The characteristic colour (orange-red to pale coral) and flavour come from the shells, which are roasted to develop deep caramelised notes, then simmered in liquid to extract their sweetness. Brandy or cognac is flambéed with the shells early in the process to remove alcohol while adding depth. The soup is thickened classically either with cream alone or with rice added to the soup and puréed. The version here uses a pre-cooked lobster (widely available) and focuses the technique on extracting maximum flavour from the shells, making it practical to produce at home without requiring a live lobster.

content.text: The roasted shells are the source of all the flavour; give them enough time in the oven to be deeply golden and fragrant. Strain the soup through a very fine sieve and press the solids hard to extract as much liquid as possible. The cream goes in last; do not boil the soup after adding it.

items.preparation: cooked; meat removed and reserved; shells and heads kept for the bisque

content.text: Heat the oven to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6. Spread the lobster shells and heads in a roasting tin, drizzle with olive oil, and roast for 20 minutes until golden and fragrant. Transfer to a large pot. Add the cognac and carefully flame it with a long match to burn off the alcohol. Add the wine and let it bubble for 1 minute.

Add the carrot, celery, onion, garlic, tomatoes, tomato purée, bay leaves, thyme, and 1.2 litres of water. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 30 minutes. Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the shells hard with the back of a spoon. Return the liquid to the pan. Simmer to reduce by a third.

Season with salt, pepper, and cayenne. Add the cream and heat gently without boiling. Roughly chop the reserved lobster meat and warm briefly in the soup. Serve in warmed bowls with a portion of lobster meat in each.
